```plato
//==
// # Primitives
//
// The types the Plato compiler assumes to exist BY NAME. Their representation comes
// from the runtime, not from these declarations, so none of them can be defined in
// Plato itself - which is exactly what the `primitive` keyword records (plato-367).
// Everything else in this vocabulary is an ordinary `type` whose shape is its
// declaration.
//
// Fields are intentionally absent throughout: a primitive has no declarable shape.
// What each declaration DOES carry is its interface surface - the `implements` list
// states which foundational interfaces the intrinsic satisfies, and that is the only
// authority the checker has over these names.
//
// The set below is the whole set. Adding a declaration here is a claim that the
// compiler and every backend must know the name; see
// `Plato.Compiler/Types/WriterPrimitiveNames.cs` for the writer-side mirror and
// plato-365 for the standing effort to keep the set as small as possible.

// ## Scalars

// A real number, approximated by the arithmetic of the compilation's Number profile
// (docs/SEMANTICS.md section 1): IEEE 754 binary64 under cpu64, the default, and binary32
// under gpu32. One profile holds for the whole program; there is no second floating type.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IEEE_754)
primitive Number
    implements IReal
{ }
```
